subject: math

objective.text: Split rectangles and circles into 2 equal parts. Each part is a half.

source_ref.section: Lesson objective: Partition circles and rectangles into equal parts, and describe those parts as halves, thirds, or fourths.

explanations.title: Halves by folding
explanations.text: Fold a paper so both sides match. Now there are 2 equal parts. Each part is a half.

explanations.title: Two halves make a whole
explanations.text: Cut on the fold. Hold the 2 halves. Put them together. Now you have 1 whole again.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: cutting along the fold

explanations.title: Equal parts, any direction
explanations.text: Turn the circle. The line can go any way. If the 2 parts are equal, they are halves.

explanations.title: Fair shares
explanations.text: Think of a pizza. If 2 parts are not the same size, they are not fair shares. They are not halves.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: shaded shapes discussion (Shape B)

examples.title: Three parts that are not equal
examples.text: Shape C has 3 parts. The parts are not equal. So it is not halves, and it is not thirds.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: shaded shapes discussion (Shape C)

misconceptions.label: Any 2 parts are halves
misconceptions.description: Child calls a shape split into 2 parts 'halves' even when the parts are not the same size.
detection_signals: Says 'halves' or 'yes' for a shape with 2 unequal parts.
Does not mention equal size when explaining halves.
misconceptions.response_text: Halves are 2 equal parts. These parts are different sizes, so they are not halves.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: Shape B ('it wouldn't be fair shares')

misconceptions.label: Thinking the line direction decides halves
misconceptions.description: Child thinks only an up-and-down (or across) line makes halves, or that turning the shape changes it.
detection_signals: Says a turned or slanted half-line does not make halves.
Says a circle can be cut in half only one way.
misconceptions.response_text: Turn it any way. If the 2 parts are equal, they are still halves.

source_ref.section: Concept Development: 'halves are determined by equal parts not by the orientation of the line'
